views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Keep the already-announced 1 June rate hike on the existing ~$60B U.S. list in force as the proportionate answer to the 10 May List 3 increase, but do not add a new tariff list or fire an immediate non-tariff blast (rare earths, Treasury sales, mass licensing delays) in response to yesterday’s Huawei order. Invite Lighthizer/Mnuchin back to Beijing and keep a G20/Osaka channel open, without new legal-change, unilateral-enforcement, or purchase concessions while Washington is still hiking and blacklisting. Use the weeks before 1 June and before any $300B list is finalized to test whether the U.S. will trade a pause for talks; if Commerce actually severs Huawei’s U.S. supply, reserve a calibrated non-tariff response then.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is high, not existential. Combined U.S. Section 301 coverage is now ~$250B at 25% after List 3 rose from 10% to 25% on 10 May, and the White House has directed preparation of tariffs on the remaining ~$300B (timeline 2019-05-05, 2019-05-10). That is a material hit to export hubs. The 15 May EO 13873 plus Commerce’s move to put Huawei and ~70 affiliates on the Entity List is firm-level targeting of a national champion and a direct strike on tech self-sufficiency (timeline 2019-05-15; Reuters/Skadden). The yuan has already slipped from ~6.73 in early May to 6.8742 on 15 May, with spot prints near 6.90 and talk of 7 — FX pressure is real (DEXCHUS; Reuters 13 May). Morgan Stanley’s contemporaneous estimate that the latest hike could trim ~0.5pp of Chinese growth (up to ~1pp if the $300B list lands) sits next to the +0.5 CHN threat anchor (major export sectors, FX, Huawei, unemployment risk). It is not +1.0: industrial production is still +5.0% YoY, reserves are ~$3.12T and slightly up, merchandise exports remain large, and the discount rate is unchanged — no financial-stability break yet (CHNPRINTO01IXPYM, TRESEGCNM052N, XTEXVA01CNM667S).

Action should not automatically escalate. China already announced the mirror tariff move on 13 May (5–25% on ~$60B, mostly 1 June), and Beijing is running out of U.S. goods to tax. A further blast after the Huawei order would likely accelerate the remaining $300B list and deepen the growth/FX hit, while conceding on enforceable legal changes or large extra purchases would reward coercion after Washington hiked mid-talks (Liu He: remove extra tariffs, balanced text, purchases tied to real demand; talks called a “small setback,” door still open). Negotiate without new commitments is the stance that answers the tariff hike, keeps a path off the $300B cliff, and does not pretend Huawei is costless.
key_factors: List 3 now 25% on ~$200B; remaining ~$300B list in preparation
Huawei Entity List + EO 13873 (15 May) hits a national champion and tech autonomy
CNY slide from ~6.73 to ~6.87–6.90; analysts flag 7 as a capital-outflow line
June 1 retaliation on ~$60B already announced; China is short of further U.S. import ammunition
Talks collapsed over enforcement/legal changes and tariff-offramps, but Liu He left a Beijing/G20 channel open
Real economy not broken: IP ~+5% YoY, reserves ~$3.12T, exports still large
Further non-tariff escalation risks bringing the $300B list forward; concession now rewards mid-talks coercion

sources_cited.excerpt: Trump tweets negotiations going too slowly and China attempting to renegotiate; orders List 3 raised from 10% to 25% on May 10 and directs preparation of tariffs on remaining Chinese imports (~$300B).
List 3 tariff rate rises from 10% to 25%.
China announces it will raise retaliatory tariff rates on its ~$60B US-goods list (higher rates phased in; many effective June 1).
Trump signs Executive Order 13873 (securing information/communications technology supply chains). Commerce moves to restrict Huawei.
CNY/USD 6.8742 on 2019-05-15, up from ~6.73 in early May (6.7319 on 1 May; 6.8765 on 13 May).
China industrial production still +5.0% YoY as of 2019-05-01 (down from 105.7 in Dec 2018).
China reserves ex-gold ~$3.12T as of 2019-05-01, slightly higher over the window.
Commerce added Huawei and 70 affiliates to the Entity List; U.S. officials said this could make it difficult or impossible for Huawei to sell some products given reliance on U.S. suppliers.
China raises duties on $60B of U.S. goods from 1 June (25/20/10/5% tiers); CCTV: if you want to talk the door is open, if you want to fight we will fight to the end.
Liu He: U.S. must remove extra tariffs for a deal; purchase targets must match real demand; text must be balanced; both sides will meet again in Beijing; he is optimistic.
Morgan Stanley: latest U.S. duties could knock 0.5pp off China growth, up to 1pp if both sides extend penalties to all exports; Q1 growth held at 6.4%.
Yuan fell ~0.8% to 6.9040 on 13 May, weakest since late December; analysts said it may breach 7; China likely to defend 7 with reserves.
